_what: One real OpenCode request per surface, recorded through a local forward proxy and reduced to the parts a contract test may assert.
_how: The real OpenCode CLI was driven in a scratch HOME/XDG tree with provider.opencode.options.baseURL pointed at a recording proxy on 127.0.0.1; the credential came from the environment and was never written to the user's own OpenCode config. The responses capture answered 200 text/event-stream. The chat-completions capture is the same model, key and headers sent to the other endpoint minutes later by a scripted probe, which answered 500.
_retake_when: Any opencode-ai major, or whenever the OpenCode surface work is touched. A fixture pins MCC to ONE observation: it catches MCC drifting away from OpenCode, never OpenCode drifting away from the fixture.
_not_asserted: Authorization, per-call ids (x-opencode-request, x-opencode-session), the x-stainless-* family MCC's SDK adds, and transport headers. The first is a secret, the second changes every call, the third carries the runner's Python and OS versions and fails on a different machine, and the fourth is the HTTP client's business.
